summary: The @gyomu/ui-core package provides a robust framework for automated form generation and UI error management. It bridges the gap between raw data schemas and interactive user interfaces by providing domain-specific language structures, schema-driven validation, and centralized error handling logic.
responsibilities: Orchestrate the automated generation of form structures from structural schemas.
Centralize UI-related error handling, categorization, and recovery strategies.
Define domain-specific metadata for form fields and UI configurations.
Manage form state lifecycle, including initialization of default values and field validation.
Provide a unified interface for linking data schemas to interactive React-based UI components.

capabilities.name: Automated Form Generation
capabilities.description: Enables the dynamic creation of form structures and field metadata directly from structural schema definitions.

capabilities.name: Schema-Driven Validation
capabilities.description: Provides mechanisms to validate field inputs and complete form states against CRUD-compliant schemas.

capabilities.name: UI Error Orchestration
capabilities.description: Standardizes how UI errors are categorized, configured, and handled, including support for retry logic and user feedback.

capabilities.name: Component Rendering Framework
capabilities.description: Maps widget configurations to specific React components, enabling consistent rendering and interaction handling.

designDecisions: Utilizes a schema-first approach where UI structures are derived from persistent data models to ensure consistency.
Decouples error handling logic from specific components using a context-based registry and handler map pattern.
Employs a DSL-based translation layer to bridge the gap between technical data definitions and user-facing form metadata.
Leverages the Effect ecosystem for robust functional error management and operational consistency.
usageGuidance: Define your data models using the @gyomu/schema package to ensure seamless integration with the automated form engine.
Configure custom error handlers within the application initialization phase to maintain consistent user feedback across the system.
Use the DSL transformation utilities when you need to extend base schema definitions with application-specific UI annotations.
Register your custom React components in the RendererMap to maintain control over the look and feel while leveraging the automated engine.
